questions.question: Which of the following pairs is associated with the taxation system of the Marathas?
questions.solution:
__**Chauth and Sardeshmukh**__ are associated with the taxation system of the** Marathas.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Chauth was a daily tax or tribute levied by the Maratha Empire, from the beginning of the 18th century. This was a nominally levied annual tax on profits or output at 25 percent.
 
• It was levied on the lands that were under** Mughal nominal control. **
 
• The sardeshmukh was on top of the chauth an **extra 10 percent tax.**
 
• It was initiated by **Koli Maharaja Som Shah of Ramnagar.**

questions.question: The Arid Forest Research Institute is located in ______.
questions.solution:
**The Arid Forest Research Institute **is located in **__Jodhpur.__**

 
• In the** hot arid and semi-arid regions of Rajasthan and Gujarat,** the Institute conducts scientific research in forestry to provide technologies to increase the vegetative cover and to preserve biodiversity.
 
• It functions under the **Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE)**(Ministry of Environment and Forests).
 
• It was established in **1988.**
 
• The Institute is headed by the Director, with the assistance of a Group Manager (Research) and Facilities Manager.

questions.question: With which sport is Archana Kamath associated?
questions.solution:
**Archana Kamath **is associated with **__Table Tennis__**.

questions.question: Which female Indian cricketer won the BCCI C.K. Nayudu Lifetime Achievement Award for 2019?

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with reference to the Karachi Session of the Congress (1931)?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the session
The Khilafat movement was launched at this event

questions.solution:
The Congress approved __**the Gandhi Irwin Agreement**__ in the** Karachi Session of 1931.**

questions.question: The first electron shell which is the nearest to the nucleus never holds more than 'n' electrons, where 'n' is equal to:
questions.solution:
**The first electron** shell which is the nearest to the nucleus never holds more than 'n' electrons, where 'n' is equal to __**2**__.

__
 
• **Electrons** are part of the lepton particle family's first generation, and are usually considered to be elementary particles since they have no established components or substructure.
 
• It has a mass which is around **1/1836 that of the proton**.
 
• The electron is discovered by **J. J. Thomson.**__
 
• **Danish physicist Niels Bohr** postulated in 1913 that electrons existed in quantized states of space, with their energies determined by the angular momentum of the orbit of the electron around the nucleus.

questions.question: The Act that transferred the power from the British East India Company to the British Crown in India was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act, 1858**__.

__
 
• **The Act that transferred the power from the British East India Company to the British Crown in India was the Government of India Act, 1858**__.

 
 
• This was an Act passed by the **British Parliament on 2 August 1858.**
 
• **Lord Palmerston,** then United Kingdom Prime Minister, proposed a bill for the transfer of power from the East India Company to the Crown by the Government of India.
 
• **The Indian Rebellion of 1857** compelled the British Government to enact the Act.
 
• The Crown was empowered to name a **Governor-General and presidential governors.**

questions.question: Which among the following is the food tube?
questions.solution:
__**Oesophagus**__ is the **food tube.**

 
• It is an organ in vertebrates, by which food travels from the pharynx to the stomach, aided by peristaltic contractions.
 
• This is a** fibromuscular tube **with an adult length of around 25 centimetres.
 
• This is one of the** upper digestive system elements.**
 
• Nutrition is absorbed through the mouth and passes through the pharynx first, and then into the **oesophagus when swallowed.**

questions.question: In which year was NABARD established?
questions.solution:

• It was formed to enforce the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act 1981 on 12 July 1982 on the recommendations of the **B.Sivaramman Committee, (by Parliament Act 61, 1981).**
 
• It is the** India's Agriculture and Rural Development Specialized Bank.**
 
• The headquarters is situated in** Mumbai.**

questions.question: How many degrees does the Earth rotate about its own axis in one hour?
questions.solution:
**The Earth rotate **about its own axis in one hour is **__15 degree.__**

 
• **The Earth circles the sun, **and in counter-clockwise motion revolves on its axis.
 
• It too rotates at an **hourly speed of 1042 miles.**
 
• The Earth rotates 360 degrees on its axis every 24 hours. Perhaps you might look at it like it takes a day to full a complete circle.
 
• The Earth rotates 15 degrees an hour, split into **an hourly rate (360/24).**

questions.question: Which of the following states does NOT share its boundary with Bhutan?
questions.solution:

questions.question: In July 2019, which among the following operations was launched by the BSF to fortify the Pakistan border in Punjab and Jammu?
questions.solution:
**In July 2019, Sudarshan operation** was launched by the BSF to fortify the **Pakistan border in Punjab and Jammu.**

 
• The exercise is called **Sudarshan **drawing from Lord Krishna's Sudarshan Chakra (or mythological wheel).
 
• It will span the entire length of India-Pakistan International Border over 1,000 km with which Jammu shares approximately 485 km of Pakistan border.
 
• **On 1 December 1965**, in the wake of the 1965 war between India and Pakistan, the Border Security Force was established to ensure the security of India's borders and related matters.
 
• It is an administratively managed government agency of the **Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).**

questions.question: Under which of the following Amendments to the Constitution of India is defection to another party after election made illegal?
questions.solution:
**Under __52ⁿd__ Amendments to the Constitution of India **is defection to another party after election made illegal.

 
• The Bill aims to change the Constitution in order to provide for an elected Member of Parliament or a Legislature of State.
 
• **The 61st Amendment to Constitution of India,** formally known as the **Constitution Act 1988**, reduced the voting age of elections to the Lok Sabha and the state legislatures from 21 years to 18 years.
 
• **The 92ⁿd Amendment to Constitution of India **amended the Constitution's Eighth Schedule to include the languages of Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santali, bringing the total number of languages mentioned in the schedule to 22.

questions.question: The Battle of Chausa was fought between Humayun and which of the following ruler?
questions.solution:
The **Battle of Chausa** was fought between **Humayun** and __**Sher Shah Suri**__.

 
• It was fought at **Chausa, **10 miles southwest of Buxar, in modern-day Bihar, India, on 26 June 1539.
 
• Humayun fled the battlefield to save his own life. Sher Shah was triumphant, and Farīd al-Dīn Shēr Shah himself was crowned.
 
• **Sher Shah Suri** was the** founder of the Suri Empire.**
 
• He had introduced the **rupee/rupiah** currency.

questions.question: Which of the following is a heritage site of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Bhimbetka**__

__
 
• **Bhimbetka**__ is a heritage site of **Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• **The Bhimbetka rock shelters** in central India are an archeological site spanning the prehistoric Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods as well as the historical period.
 
• It is situated in the **Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• It is a **UNESCO world heritage site** containing seven hills.
 
• This is one of the most important prehistoric complexes.

questions.question: The SASTRA - Ramanujan Prize is awarded in the field of ________.
questions.solution:
**The SASTRA - Ramanujan Prize** is awarded in the field of __**Mathematics.**__

 
• It is established by the **Shanmugha Academy of Arts, Science, Technology and Research (SASTRA) near Kumbakonam, India,**
 
• It is awarded annually to a young mathematician who is considered to have done outstanding research in the fields of interest in Ramanujan.
 
• The age limit for the reward was set at 32 (the age Ramanujan died at), and the new award is $10,000.
 
• Srinivasa Ramanujan made important contributions to **mathematical analysis, number theory, infinite series, and continuous fractions, including solutions **to mathematical problems that were then considered unsolvable.

questions.question: Ozone at the higher level of the atmosphere is a product of ______ acting on oxygen molecules.
questions.solution:
**Ozone** at the higher level of the atmosphere is a product of __**UV radiation**__ acting on **oxygen molecules.**

 
• Ultraviolet (UV) is electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength from 10 nm to 400 nm, shorter than that of visible light but longer than X-rays.
 
• It emitted by the Sun and is absorbed by oxygen and creates ozone in the ozone layer when single oxygen atoms emitted by dioxygen photolysis react with greater dioxygen.
 
• It has a **higher frequency than violet light** (and hence a shorter wavelength).

questions.question: In January 2020, with which country did India sign a MoU for content exchange programme between All India Radio and Betar?
questions.solution:
In **January 2020**, India did sign an **MoU** with __**Bangladesh**__ for a content exchange program between** All India Radio and Betar.**

 
• A** Memorandum of understanding(MoU) **is a kind of agreement between two (bilateral) or more (multilateral) parties.
 
• It communicates a cohesion of will between the parties, which implies a shared course of action expected.
 
• This is also used in cases where parties do not indicate a legal obligation or in circumstances where the parties are unable to create a legally enforceable contract.
 
• It is a more formal alternative to** an arrangement between gentlemen.**

questions.question: Under which Article can the Parliament amend the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Under the **Article 368**, the parliament can **amend the Constitution**.

 
• **Amending the constitution of India** is the process of making amendments to the fundamental law or supreme law of the country.
 
• The amendment process in the constitution is set out in** Part XX (Article 368) of the Indian Constitution. **
 
• This procedure preserves the sanctity of India's Constitution and holds a check on the Indian Parliament's arbitrary power.
 
• Article 368 does not set down the legislative process to be followed at various points of the amendment.
